desc:
The array nums has an even length 2n. One riffle splits it into the first half a = nums[0..n-1] and the second half b = nums[n..2n-1] and interleaves them, starting with the first half: [a[0], b[0], a[1], b[1], ..., a[n-1], b[n-1]].

Apply the riffle t times in a row and return the final array. t can be huge, so you cannot afford to simulate every shuffle.

nums = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6], t = 1  result = [1, 4, 2, 5, 3, 6]
nums = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6], t = 2  result = [1, 5, 4, 3, 2, 6]
hints: Simulating t shuffles costs O(n * t). Notice that every riffle moves each position to the same new position, no matter what values it holds.
Position p moves to 2p if p < n, and to 2(p - n) + 1 otherwise. This is a permutation of positions, so it splits into cycles.
Walk each cycle of positions once, in the order of the moves. In a cycle of length L, applying the riffle t times moves the element at the cycle's k-th position to the (k + t) mod L-th position.
editorial: A shuffle is a fixed permutation of positions. Applying it t times is the permutation raised to the power t, and a permutation is easiest to power through its cycle decomposition: inside a cycle of length L, t steps are equivalent to t mod L steps.

Define dest(p) = 2p for p < n and 2(p - n) + 1 otherwise. Visit every unvisited position, follow dest to collect its cycle c[0], c[1], ..., c[L-1] (so dest(c[k]) = c[k+1]), and place the value from c[k] at c[(k + t) mod L] of the result.

Every position is visited once, so the running time is O(n), independent of t, and the extra space is O(n) for the visited flags and the answer. (The cycle structure is the classic perfect-shuffle one, with dest(p) = 2p mod (2n - 1) for all but the last position, but the explicit piecewise rule is enough.)
solution:
def riffleRepeated(nums, t):
    m = len(nums)
    h = m // 2
    res = [0] * m
    seen = [False] * m
    for s in range(m):
        if seen[s]:
            continue
        cyc = []
        p = s
        while not seen[p]:
            seen[p] = True
            cyc.append(p)
            p = 2 * p if p < h else 2 * (p - h) + 1
        L = len(cyc)
        sh = t % L
        for k, pos in enumerate(cyc):
            res[cyc[(k + sh) % L]] = nums[pos]
    return res
